claim_snippets.claim_text: In the reported experiment, GPT-5.3-Codex ran for about 25 hours and executed verification steps such as tests, lint, and typecheck for every completed milestone.
Prompt.md is used to freeze goals, non-goals, hard constraints, deliverables, and a 'done when' section so the agent does not drift toward an impressive but wrong target.
Plan.md turns open-ended work into checkpoints with milestones small enough for one loop, acceptance criteria, validation commands, a stop-and-fix rule, and decision notes to avoid oscillation.

records.title: Using skills to accelerate OSS maintenance
records.relevance_note: Repository rules and skill metadata are used to force verification and route workflow steps.
records.reason_included: Shows concrete if-then workflow control embedded in repo instructions and skill descriptions.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The repo uses short if/then rules in AGENTS.md so that before runtime or API edits Codex must call implementation-strategy, and if code, tests, examples, or build behavior change it must call code-change-verification.
The code-change-verification rule is conditional, but once triggered it requires formatting, lint, type-checking, and tests, and the work is not complete until that stack passes.
Skills follow a progressive-disclosure model where name and description are loaded first; in practice description becomes a main routing signal before Codex reads the rest of the skill.

records.title: Codex Prompting Guide
records.relevance_note: Gives explicit next-action and stop rules for Codex-style coding loops.
records.reason_included: Contains operational constraints on planning, loop termination, and state handoff via phase.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When using the planning tool, Codex should skip it for straightforward tasks, avoid single-step plans, update plans after subtask progress, and never end with only a plan.
Before finishing, Codex should reconcile every prior plan or TODO item and mark it Done, Blocked, or Cancelled, with no pending items left open.
The Responses API phase parameter is intended to prevent early stopping and other misbehaviors when preamble messages are used, and correct phase handling is required for gpt-5.3-codex performance.
If the agent is re-reading or re-editing the same files without clear progress, it should stop that loop and end the turn with a concise summary and any needed clarifying questions.

records.title: Automate workflows with hooks
records.exception_reason: Published after the March 24, 2026 primary-window cutoff; retained for deterministic lifecycle hooks, stop-hook continuation, and compaction reinjection mechanics.
records.relevance_note: Automate workflows with hooks is a official doc source with details on deterministic lifecycle hooks, prompt based stop hook relevant to policy program.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on policy program, verification, execution loop.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Hooks are shell commands attached to Claude Code lifecycle events and are described as deterministic control so certain actions always happen rather than depending on the LLM to choose them.
A Stop prompt hook can return ok=false with a reason, in which case Claude keeps working and uses the reason as its next instruction.
An agent-based Stop hook can spawn a subagent with tool access to verify conditions such as whether the test suite passes before allowing Claude to stop.
Stop hooks fire whenever Claude finishes responding, and if the stop_hook_active field is not checked they can cause an infinite continuation loop.

records.title: Create custom subagents
records.exception_reason: Published after the March 24, 2026 primary-window cutoff; retained for concrete subagent delegation, context isolation, and allowlist mechanics in Claude Code.
records.relevance_note: Create custom subagents is a official doc source with details on delegation by description, isolated context workers relevant to agent architecture.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions, and Claude delegates when the task matches the subagent description.
Automatic delegation is driven by the task description, the subagent description field, and current context; stronger descriptions encourage proactive delegation.
Subagent spawning can be allowlisted so only specific agent types can be created, and attempts to spawn other types fail.
Chained subagents support sequential multi-step workflows where each subagent returns results and Claude passes relevant context to the next worker.

records.title: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions
records.exception_reason: Published after the March 24, 2026 primary-window cutoff; retained for concrete team task-claiming, dependency unblocking, and approval-gated workflow mechanics.
records.relevance_note: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions is a official doc source with details on shared task list, self claim scheduler relevant to agent architecture.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on topology, execution loop, state.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Agent teams coordinate through a shared task list with self-coordination, while each teammate has its own context window and can communicate directly with other teammates.
For risky work, teammates can be forced into read-only plan mode until the lead approves the plan; rejected plans stay in plan mode, are revised, and resubmitted.
Tasks have states pending, in progress, and completed, can depend on other tasks, and teammates can self-claim the next unassigned unblocked task; file locking prevents simultaneous claims.
When a teammate completes a task, blocked dependent tasks unblock automatically, and teams can add quality gates via hooks that prevent task completion or keep a teammate working.
Agent teams add coordination overhead and significantly more token cost; for sequential tasks or same-file edits, a single session or subagents are more effective.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In auto mode, the classifier receives user messages and tool calls plus CLAUDE.md, but Claude’s own text and tool results are stripped out so hostile file or web content cannot directly manipulate the classifier.
Subagent spawns are evaluated by the classifier, and subagent tool calls are independently classified under the same block and allow rules when auto mode is inherited.
If the classifier blocks an action three times in a row or twenty times total in one session, auto mode falls back to prompting for each action.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Action schemas define a small explicit set of allowed actions so an agent must return one valid action instead of improvising intent.
MCP enforces explicit input and output schemas for every tool and resource and validates calls before execution, preventing bad state from reaching production systems.

claim_snippets.claim_text: OpenHands V1 makes agents, tools, and LLMs immutable and keeps a single conversation state object as the one mutable source of truth, enabling deterministic replay, strong consistency, and stable recovery.
The SDK uses an event-sourced state model with deterministic replay and a typed tool system with MCP integration.
The agent is a stateless event processor whose design supports security interleaving, incremental one-step execution, pause/resume, recovery from context overflows, and event streaming.
OpenHands adds stuck detection for repeated same-action loops and redundant tool calls and can terminate execution automatically to prevent resource waste.

records.title: Agent
records.exception_reason: Published after the March 24, 2026 primary-window cutoff; retained for the ordered single-step reasoning-action loop and condensation-request mechanics in the OpenHands SDK.
records.relevance_note: Agent is a official doc source with details on single step execution model, pending action priority relevant to execution control.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on execution loop, state, context.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The agent runs a single-step execution model: pending actions first, then condensation, then LLM query, response parsing, confirmation checks, and finally action execution.
If the context window is exceeded during the LLM query stage, the agent emits a CondensationRequest and returns rather than continuing the loop blindly.
The agent is stateless and event-driven: it reads from event history, writes new events, and each step is atomic so execution can be paused and resumed.
Before execution, a security analyzer evaluates action risk and can trigger confirmation or blocking behavior for higher-risk actions.

records.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
records.relevance_note: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces is a paper source with details on containerized task harness, end state tests relevant to evals benchmarking.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on eval design, verification, execution loop.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Terminal-Bench 2.0 contains 89 terminal tasks, each with a unique environment, a human-written solution, and comprehensive tests for verification; frontier systems solve less than 65% of tasks.
Premature termination is defined as declaring completion before meeting explicit objectives or before delivering required artifacts or verification.
Weak verification means the checks do not cover properties required for true correctness, while no or incorrect verification includes bypassing a designated verifier or ignoring failing core checks.
Average episode count has negligible correlation with success rate, indicating that simply taking more interaction rounds does not predict solving the task.

records.title: Verified Multi-Agent Orchestration: A Plan-Execute-Verify-Replan Framework for Complex Query Resolution
records.relevance_note: Explicit verify-replan orchestration with stop conditions and dependency fields.
records.reason_included: Strong source for verifier-led continuation and stop-policy design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: VMAO runs through Plan, Execute, Verify, Replan, and Synthesize phases, where verification evaluates completeness and deficiencies trigger new sub-questions or retries.
Sub-questions carry explicit fields including id, agent_type, dependencies, priority, context_from_deps, and verification_criteria.
After each verification phase, five configurable stop conditions are checked: completeness threshold, high confidence with partial coverage, diminishing returns, token budget, and maximum iterations.

records.title: A Dual-Loop Agent Framework for Automated Vulnerability Reproduction
records.relevance_note: A Dual-Loop Agent Framework for Automated Vulnerability Reproduction is a paper source with details on dual loop control, strategic tactical separation relevant to recovery fault tolerance.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on recovery, verification, execution loop.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Cve2PoC uses a dual-loop design: the Strategic Planner makes structured attack plans, the Tactical Executor performs code generation with progressive verification, and the Adaptive Refiner routes failures either to tactical refinement or strategic replanning.
Removing the Adaptive Refiner causes a 23.2 percentage point drop in reproduction success rate on SecBench.js and leads to repeated ineffective debugging loops.
The framework argues that naive experience injection inflates context, so it indexes prior attempts by failure characteristics for sparse retrieval relevant to the current failure.
